title: Y90 Radioembolization Therapy
summary: Y90 radioembolization therapy guidance for hepatic malignancy treatment, radiation lobectomy, bridge therapy, and palliative disease control.
provenance: Imported from procedure orders PDF updated 4.15.26
reviewNotes: Confirm local Y90 activity and dosimetry workflow.
Confirm SIR-Sphere and TheraSphere lung shunt/lung dose policy.
Confirm nuclear medicine handoff and scheduling workflow.
Confirm one-month MRI liver mass and lab workflow.

blocks.text: Hepatic malignancy treatment, bridge therapy, radiation lobectomy, or palliation.

items: Unresectable or recurrent HCC.
Metastatic disease to the liver.
Radiation lobectomy to treat tumor and induce contralateral hypertrophy.
Bridge to transplant/resection.
Palliative disease control.

blocks.text: High bleeding risk; hold anticoagulants/antiplatelets per policy.

items: High bleeding risk.
Warfarin: hold 5 days and confirm INR <= 1.8.
IV unfractionated heparin: hold 4-6 hours and check aPTT or anti-Xa level.
Enoxaparin: hold 1 dose if prophylactic; hold 2 doses or 24 hours if therapeutic.
DOAC timing is agent-, dose-, and renal-function-specific; use the anticoagulation table.
Clopidogrel and ticagrelor: hold 5 days; prasugrel: hold 7 days.
Aspirin: hold 3-5 days.
CBC.
INR.
CMP.
AFP.
Platelets >50k.

blocks.text: Procedure-specific pre-procedure orders have not yet been documented in this guide.

items: Moderate sedation.

blocks.text: Confirm indication, mapping anatomy, labs, cone-beam CT, nuclear medicine scheduling, and lung shunt thresholds.

items: Confirm sedation plan - patient can lie flat.

blocks.title: Core checklist
items: Confirm indication.
Review anatomy from Y90 mapping study.
Labs are appropriate.
CT cone beam available.
Nuclear medicine aware and scheduled.

blocks.title: Lung shunt fraction from Tc-99m mapping scan
items: < 10% - acceptable.
10-20% - elevated; calculate predicted lung dose and potentially reduce Y90 activity.
> 20% - contraindication for SIR-Sphere resin microspheres.

blocks.title: TheraSphere glass microspheres
items: No percentage cutoff for TheraSphere glass microspheres; lung dose is the metric.
< 30 Gy per treatment.
< 50 Gy cumulative.
match the planned segment or lobe and all intended tumor feeders.
reproduce the mapping location relative to arterial branches; small shifts can change distribution.
recheck gastric, duodenal, and cystic branches; collateral flow may have changed.
shunted particles can irradiate lungs; use the approved mapping-based plan.
preserve adequate functioning liver; lobar and segmental treatment expose different volumes.
review interval labs, mapping, product, treatment territory, and approved dose plan.
verify patient, vial/activity, calibration time, and intended artery with the authorized team.
and confirm target perfusion and safe forward flow with angiography.
through the product-specific system; monitor flow and stop for reflux or stasis.
per protocol; measure residual activity to document what was actually delivered.
with Y90 PET/CT or bremsstrahlung SPECT/CT per local protocol; secure arterial hemostasis.
microspheres lodge in small vessels and release short-range beta radiation; the main effect is radiation, not simply blocking blood flow.
GBq describes radioactivity administered; Gy describes energy absorbed by tissue. Distribution links the two.
post-treatment imaging shows where the particles went, not whether the tumor has already responded.
do not use the old plan blindly; reassess and remap if the intended delivery no longer matches.
stop and reassess; never force the remaining activity through a poorly flowing catheter.
independently verify each planned administration; glass and resin systems are not interchangeable.
persistent abdominal pain or GI bleeding warrants evaluation for radiation injury, not just routine post-treatment symptoms.
new jaundice, ascites, cough, or dyspnea may be delayed; escalate and assess radiation-related injury.
document residual activity and follow radiation-safety procedures for leaks, spills, and disposal.

blocks.text: Routine orders, access recovery, anticoagulation restart, discharge, AVS, and one-month follow-up.

blocks.title: Routine orders
items: Regular diet.
Tylenol 650 mg PRN.
Vital signs - Every 15 minutes x 4, then every 30 minutes x 2, then every 1 hour x 4, then every 4 hours; edit to match bedrest.

blocks.title: Femoral access
items: Bedrest for 2 hours with leg flat.
Monitor color of access site.

blocks.title: Radial access
items: Activity per JH-HLM mobility goal.
Monitor color of access site.
Remove radial artery compression device.

blocks.title: Anticoagulation to resume
items: Warfarin: resume the day after the procedure; bridging requires individualized multidisciplinary planning.
IV unfractionated heparin: 6-8 hours after the procedure.
Enoxaparin: 12 hours after the procedure.
Apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, and edoxaban: Table 6 lists 24 hours; confirm renal function and local policy before restarting.
Clopidogrel: 6 hours after the procedure for a 75-mg dose or 24 hours for a 300-600-mg loading dose.
Ticagrelor, prasugrel, and aspirin: resume the day after the procedure.
Restart only after procedural bleeding risk is controlled; traumatic, neuraxial, multi-agent, and high-thrombosis-risk cases need individualized review.

blocks.title: Discharge
items: Discharge order with medication reconciliation prior - 2-6 hours.
After visit summary: .IRAVSY901.

blocks.title: Follow up
items: Clinic visit in 1 month with MRI liver mass and labs: CBC, INR, CMP, AFP.
